Prepare the request body ```json { "type": "vote", "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious" } } ``` > **Tip:** If you want to add a comment or a reason, you can extend the `attributes` object: > ```json > { > "type": "vote", > "attributes": { > "verdict": "malicious", > "comment": "This IP was observed sending spam emails." > } > } > ``` --- ## 2. Build the HTTP request | Element | Value | |---------|-------| | Method | `POST` | | URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/votes/ip/22.242.75.136` | | Headers | `x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY`
`Content-Type: application/json` | | Body | The JSON from Step 1 | ### Example using `curl` ```bash curl -X POST \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/votes/ip/22.242.75.136 \ -H "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"type":"vote","attributes":{"verdict":"malicious"}}' ``` ### Example using `Python` (`requests` library) ```python import requests url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/votes/ip/22.242.75.136" headers = { "x-apikey": "YOUR_API_KEY", "Content-Type": "application/json" } payload = { "type": "vote", "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious" } } response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` --- ## 3. Interpret the response | Status Code | Meaning | |-------------|---------| | `200` | Vote accepted. The response will contain the vote ID and timestamp. | | `201` | Vote created successfully (some APIs return 201). | | `400` | Bad request – usually malformed JSON or missing fields. | | `401` | Unauthorized – wrong or missing API key. | | `403` | Forbidden – you don’t have permission to vote on this resource. | | `404` | Not found – the IP address does not exist in the database. | | `429` | Rate limit exceeded – wait before retrying. | | `500` | Server error – try again later. | A successful response looks like: ```json { "data": { "id": "1234567890abcdef", "type": "vote", "attributes": { "verdict": "malicious", "date": "2026-07-07T12:34:56Z", "ip_address": "22.242.75.136" } } } ``` --- ## 4. Verify the vote After submitting, you can retrieve the vote record to confirm it was stored: ```bash curl -X GET \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/votes/ip/22.242.75.136 \ -H "x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY" ``` If you see the same `verdict` and `ip_address` in the response, the vote has been recorded. --- ## 5. Common pitfalls & troubleshooting | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **API key not working** | Double‑check that you’re using the *public* API key, not the *private* one. | | **Wrong endpoint** | Ensure the URL ends with `/votes/ip/`. | | **Missing `x-apikey` header** | The key must be sent in the header, not in the query string. | | **Rate limiting** | If you hit `429`, back off for at least 60 seconds before retrying. | | **JSON formatting errors** | Use a linter or online validator to confirm the JSON is valid. | --- ## 6. Security reminder - Never expose your API key in logs, scripts, or shared documents. - Store it in environment variables or a secrets manager. - Rotate keys periodically and revoke any that may have leaked. --- ### Quick checklist 1. Replace `YOUR_API_KEY` with your real key. 2. Confirm the IP address (`22.242.75.136`) is correct. 3. Run the `curl` or Python snippet. 4. Check the status code and response body. 5.
